A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANPM and decentralized PCA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original synthetic ANPM experiments and decentralized evaluations on Fed-Heart-Disease and Ego-Facebook.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain original empirical evaluations and add digits and Amazon0302 experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the gossip summation from neighbors N_i to N_i union {i}, including the agent's self-weight. This changes the update as written. The ANPM recurrence, ADePM outer updates, and adaptive-momentum heuristics otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds handwritten-digits decentralized PCA with homogeneous and label-separated client populations, and spectral clustering on the large Amazon0302 graph. These substantially broaden coverage beyond the retained synthetic, Fed-Heart-Disease, and Ego-Facebook evaluations.

E2.justification: The empirical comparators remain NPM for ANPM and DePM and DeEPCA for ADePM. Added benchmarks use existing comparators; additional momentum values are settings of the same method.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 changes the synthetic spectrum from lambda_1=5, lambda_k=1 to lambda_1=lambda_k=1. Figures 1 and 3 expand momentum and eigengap grids and revise the noise sweep. Figure 2 replaces Fed-Heart-Disease's L=5/10 settings with the shared L=20/40 settings. The new Amazon experiment uses rank 30, two Gaussian noise levels, and reconstruction error, plotted relative to lambda_{k+1}, instead of principal-angle error.

E4.justification: V2 extends momentum sensitivity to values above the optimum and at the critical boundary, adds a controlled client-heterogeneity comparison on digits, and tests noise-dependent acceleration on Amazon0302. These add substantive robustness questions. The original centered-noise analysis is retained in Appendix E.2.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The additional curves do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds digits results showing worse final accuracy with heterogeneous clients, with M approximately 725 versus 230. Amazon results show faster adaptive ANPM convergence at sigma=0.001 but similar performance to NPM at sigma=0.002. Revised synthetic results include nonconvergence at the critical momentum and no significant noise-dependent transient-rate change, replacing v1's delayed-transient observation under different settings. Figures 1–3 also contain revised curves.

T1.justification: The main theorem statements and most proofs remain. Section 2.1 revises the sufficient noise condition to use initial alignment with an additional precision restriction. Lemma C.11 adds a bound for Delta>=1/2, used through a new piecewise constant in Theorem C.14's proof. However, the added bound f(Delta)<=sqrt(3)-sqrt(2)<1 contradicts the retained f(Delta)>=1. These are localized mathematical revisions, not merely renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: accelerated convergence under milder noise conditions, worst-case tightness, and an accelerated decentralized PCA algorithm with comparable communication costs.

C2.justification: V2 interprets critical-momentum nonconvergence as evidence that the admissible interval is tight and links client heterogeneity to worse accuracy. It refines the explanation of nonlinear gap behavior using noise outside the next-eigenvector direction, dropping v1's suggestion of tighter tail-spectrum bounds. The practical discussion of unknown noise projections and initial alignment is also revised.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly provides a repository location for experimental code. Appendix E documents digits allocation across ten agents and ring-network weights, plus Amazon graph size, rank, and Gaussian noise levels. The Ego-Facebook construction also corrects a duplicated matrix index to specify symmetric entries. Existing decentralized tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Alpaydin and Kaynak for digits, Leskovec et al. (2007) for Amazon0302, and Tropp (2015) for matrix concentration. Proposition 3.2's attribution changes from Liu and Morse to Ye and Zhang. The broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted language corrections, corrects the intuitive principal-angle explanation, rewrites the proof sketch and noise-condition discussion, and reorganizes Appendix E into setup and additional-experiment subsections. It adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most narrative and the main section order remain.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Figures 1 and 3 become larger 2-by-2 panels with new legends and zoom insets; Figure 2 expands from two to four panels with revised styling. The standalone zoom figure is replaced by an Amazon experiment figure. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader empirical coverage, stronger sensitivity analyses, and a newly supplied code location improve support and reproducibility. However, v2 adds the contradictory bound in Lemma C.11 and uses it in the revised proof of Theorem C.14, supporting the central optimality claim. This introduces a concrete mathematical error absent from v1's lemma. The empirical gains and theoretical harm prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
